name: Automation framework leftovers
plain: Test tools leave marks on the page that a script can look for.
meaning: Selenium, PhantomJS, Playwright and Puppeteer inject helper properties or bindings into the page, such as cdc_ prefixed document keys, callPhantom, or names starting with __playwright and __pw. Bot defenses scan the window and document for these names. Operators rename or remove them with patches.

web.api: Object.keys(window) and document for names like $cdc_, __playwright*, __pw*, callPhantom, _phantom, domAutomation, __nightmare, __selenium*

steps: Page script enumerates window and document property names
Script matches them against a list of known automation names
A hit adds to a bot score

chrome.note: Names depend on the driver and its version

firefox.note: Some drivers leave marks here too

chrome_android.note: When driven by Selenium or Appium

fields.name: matchedNames
fields.range: automation related property names found on window or document

limits.headline: Can find traces of test tools left on the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It runs from page script
can: Block or challenge clients with a hit
Combine hits with the webdriver flag
cannot: Catch a tool that renames its marks
Tell a good test from a bad scrape
limits.differs: Names change between driver versions and are removed by stealth patches. Only a known name is a hit, so new tools pass until lists catch up.

story.what_it_is: Automation tools sometimes leave their own handwriting on the page. Defenders keep a list of the known handwriting.

marketing.name: WebDriver documentation
marketing.pitch: Docs describe the browser automation standard and its drivers.

story.for_you: You never see it. A normal browser has none of these names. Test tools you run may be spotted by them.
story.for_makers: Keep your list current and match exact known names, not loose patterns, to avoid false positives. Treat a hit as strong, and a miss as meaning nothing.

use_cases.example: A web firewall flags sessions that carry a cdc_ marker on the document.
A ticket seller blocks scripted browsers with Playwright marks.
A browser game bans accounts whose window has automation bindings.
An ad network discards views with PhantomJS marks.
A tester checks a bot detection page to see which marks their framework leaves.
A traffic tool flags visits with known automation names as bots.

history.change: cdc_ style ChromeDriver marks widely documented by bot detection write ups
